knownFixesFetcher--gamelib-source-gog-20: The TS test scripts the body as an object ({title:'fresh'}), which the injected get returns unparsed; the recording stores it as its JSON text (recorded/fetcher/<case>/body-1.txt, compact, key order kept). The Rust Replay fetch serves text, so the body parses to the same value. The written file is the same either way: JSON.stringify(filtered, null, 2) with no trailing newline, pinned by the sha256 in tree.json.
knownFixesFetcher--gamelib-source-leaves: The TS temp file is named <id>-<store>.json.tmp-<pid> and is renamed over the destination; the pid is not recorded. The replay checks only that no name containing '.tmp' is left in <APPFOLDER>/fixes after the write.
rule-gamelib-timeout-through-the-default: The 10 000 ms deadline belongs to the default client (axios `timeout`), not to the fetch loop: an injected get that never settles would hang the fetch. The case scripts the transport failure axios raises at the deadline (code ECONNABORTED). The Rust client sets a 10 s reqwest timeout; the replay serves the recorded exchange as a network error and compares the requested URL, the untouched stale file and the 'request failed for <url>: ' prefix of the warning, not the error text after it.
rule-default-get-asks-with-a-10000-ms-ti: `axiosCalls` records the options of the axios client (timeout 10 000, text body kept as the server sent it, every status accepted). Rust has no axios: the replay asserts the equivalent reqwest settings (10 s timeout, the body read as text and not parsed by the client, a non-2xx status handled by the caller) and the requested URL, not the option names.
rule-default-get-falls-back-to-heroic-on: As rule-default-get-asks-with-a-10000-ms-timeout-text-and-every-status-accepted; the first exchange is the GameLib 404 and the second the Heroic 200.
rule-the-fixes-folder-being-a-file-makes: The warning text after 'Known fixes fetch failed for 1: ' is Node's `Error: EEXIST: file already exists, mkdir '<path>'`. Rust's io error prints differently; the replay compares the prefix, requires a non-empty remainder naming <APPFOLDER>/fixes, and requires the fixes entry to still be the seeded file.
rule-unsafe-app-names-write-and-ask-noth: A name that merely begins with two dots ('..dots') is refused as unsafe because the check is `relative.startsWith('..')`; recorded as found (no real id starts that way, so nothing is lost). A backslash name is not recorded: on POSIX it is an ordinary filename character and on Windows it is a separator, so the golden would differ by host (see the reader slice's delta for backslash-appname-is-host-dependent).
knownFixesFetcher--guards-rejects-a-trav: tree.json holds <APPFOLDER>/fixes and its local folder only: the escape target <APPFOLDER>/escape-gog.json was never created.
knownFixesFetcher--indeterminate-gamelib: The warning ends with String(error) of the scripted Error ('Error: ETIMEDOUT'); the Rust transport error prints differently. The replay compares up to 'request failed for <url>: ' and the untouched file.
knownFixesFetcher--heroic-fallback-s-fal: The TS test scripts the Heroic body as an object; see knownFixesFetcher--gamelib-source-gog-200-overwrites-a-stale-file-heroic-not-requested.
